content: The ATP-binding cassette sub-family G member 5 (ABCG5) is a protein encoded by the ABCG5 gene in humans. This protein belongs to the ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporter superfamily, which is responsible for transporting various molecules across both extracellular and intracellular membranes. ABC transporters are categorized into seven distinct subfamilies: ABC1, MDR/TAP, MRP, ALD, OABP, GCN20, and White. The ABCG5 protein is specifically a member of the White subfamily. The protein encoded by the ABCG5 gene functions as a half-transporter, playing a critical role in regulating sterol homeostasis. It limits the absorption of sterols in the intestine and facilitates their excretion into bile. This protein is expressed in a tissue-specific manner, predominantly in the liver, colon, and intestine. The ABCG5 gene is located on chromosome 2, where it is arranged in a head-to-head orientation with its family member gene, ABCG8. Mutations in the ABCG5 gene have been implicated in pathological conditions such as sitosterolemia, a rare autosomal recessive disorder characterized by the accumulation of dietary plant sterols in the body. These mutations may also contribute to the development of atherosclerosis due to abnormal sterol accumulation.
